content.overview: When verified water or batch measurements fall outside controlled acceptance, the strongest response is a traceable hold, authorized correction or escalation—not undocumented adjustment or changing the criteria.

vocabulary.definition: Controlled status preventing use or release while identity, measurement or disposition remains unresolved.
Authorized decision about use, correction, rework, rejection or other controlled outcome.
A verified condition outside the defined acceptance criterion for the intended process or batch.

sections.title: Verify before disposition
sections.body: Confirm sample identity and meter fitness so an apparent failure is not caused by the measurement system.

sections.title: Once verified, treat the result as real
sections.body: Do not repeat tests until one happens to pass or alter the acceptance limit for convenience. Follow the controlled hold/correction/disposition process.

sections.title: Preserve the batch history
sections.body: Record source water, recipe version, material lots, additions, final volume, measurements, corrections, hold status, authorization and final disposition.

workedExamples: A verified batch remains outside approved EC acceptance after recipe reconciliation; the batch is held and escalated rather than adjusted repeatedly without traceability.
commonMistakes: Changing criteria after seeing the result.
Releasing a batch because the recipe was followed even though verified acceptance failed.
content.practicalApplication: Complete a mock out-of-acceptance investigation and disposition record.
content.summary: Verified failures require controlled disposition and a reconstructable evidence trail.
